facts.statement: The genus Palaeotodus was described by Olson in 1976.
Palaeotodus is an extinct genus belonging to the todie family Todidae.
facts.quote: Palaeotodus is an extinct genus of todies in the family Todidae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Palaeotodus date to the Lower Oligocene epoch.
The genus lived between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago during the Rupelian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Rupelian (33.9 to 27.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Palaeotodus have been found in France and the US state of Wyoming.
facts.quote: The genus has at least three species known from fossils found in France and the American state of Wyoming.

facts.statement: Palaeotodus species were larger than modern todies and similar in size to the modern tody motmot.
facts.quote: They were larger than modern todies, and closer in size to the modern living tody motmot.

facts.statement: Remains of Palaeotodus emryi show a larger body size and proportionally larger wings compared to modern todies.
facts.quote: These remains of Palaeotodus emryi indicate a larger size and proportionally larger wings than those of modern todies.

facts.statement: The species Palaeotodus emryi was described by Olson in 1976 based on Oligocene fossils from Wyoming.
facts.quote: †Palaeotodus emryi - Olson, 1976: Oligocene fossils found in Wyoming (United States).

facts.statement: The species Palaeotodus escampsiensis was described by Mourer-Chauviré in 1985 from Upper Eocene fossils in France.
facts.quote: †Palaeotodus escampsiensis - Mourer-Chauviré, 1985: Upper Eocene fossils found in France.

facts.statement: The species Palaeotodus itardiensis was described by Mourer-Chauviré in 1985 from Lower Oligocene fossils in France.
facts.quote: †Palaeotodus itardiensis - Mourer-Chauviré, 1985: Lower Oligocene fossils found in France.

rejected.statement: Palaeotodus is classified within the class Aves (birds).
